args.content:
# app — Collections Library

A tiny TypeScript library of bounded, fixed-capacity data structures.
All structures reject overflow and underflow with explicit errors.

# Stack

Parent: [app.md](../app.md)

## Responsibility

Bounded LIFO stack over a fixed capacity, backed by an array.

## Contract

- `new Stack<T>(capacity)`: capacity must be a positive integer, else
  `RangeError`.
- `push(item)`: appends to top; throws `RangeError` on overflow.
- `pop()`: removes and returns the top; throws `RangeError` on underflow.
- `peek()`: returns the top without removal; throws `RangeError` if empty.
- `size()`: current item count.

## Invariants

- `0 <= size() <= capacity` at all times.
- Last-in, first-out: `pop`/`peek` return the most recently pushed item.
- Failed `push`/`pop`/`peek` leave the stack unchanged.

# Ring

Parent: [app.md](../app.md)

## Responsibility

Fixed-capacity FIFO ring buffer backed by a preallocated array with
wrap-around head/tail indexing.

## Contract

- `new Ring<T>(capacity)`: capacity must be a positive integer, else
  `RangeError`.
- `enqueue(item)`: appends at the tail; throws `RangeError` on overflow.
- `dequeue()`: removes and returns the head; throws `RangeError` on
  underflow.
- `peek()`: returns the head without removal; throws `RangeError` if empty.
- `size()`: current item count.

## Invariants

- `0 <= size() <= capacity` at all times.
- First-in, first-out: `dequeue`/`peek` return the oldest live item.
- Indices always wrap modulo `capacity`; storage is never resized.
- Dequeued slots are cleared to `undefined` (no stale references).
- Failed `enqueue`/`dequeue`/`peek` leave the buffer unchanged.

args.note: Spec title "Ring" corresponds to the exported class Ring<T> declaration.
Responsibility statement: fixed-capacity FIFO ring buffer with head/tail state (buf, head, count fields).
Backing storage is a single preallocated array (buf field).

args.note: Invariant 0 <= size() <= capacity: the overflow guard rejects the push when length would reach capacity, so size never exceeds capacity.
size() reports items.length, the lower-bounded live item count used in the size invariant.
Items are appended to the end of the array, making the most recently pushed item the top.
pop() returns the last array element, i.e. the most recently pushed item (LIFO).
peek() returns the final array element, i.e. the most recently pushed item (LIFO).
Failed push throws before mutating items, leaving the stack unchanged.
Failed pop throws before the array is modified, leaving the stack unchanged.
Failed peek throws without mutation, leaving the stack unchanged.
